title.narrative: Promoting economic and social rights and empowering women and youths in the South and Eastern Regions of Sierra Leone

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the action is to strengthen civil society to contribute to gender equity and youth empowerment in Sierra Leone, by promoting youth and women¿s access to socio-economic rights. Generally, the Action is designed to achieve the following Specific Objectives (SO):

1. Women in all their diversity have improved access to entrepreneurship opportunities, including social entrepreneurship, alternative livelihoods and strengthened participation in the green and circular economy.

2. To improve the livelihood and employability of young women and men and increase their resilience against social and economic shocks in Bonthe and Kailahun Districts.

This action is targeting two of the poorest and least food secure districts in the country the Bonthe and Kailahun district with a high level of entrenched patriarchal system. The action aims to create an enabling socio-economic environment for women and youths to access credit, land, and economic resources through building the capacity of women¿s groups and networks to advocate for their social and economic rights and helping them access justice in relation to their socio-economic rights. By empowering women and youths through training, leadership development, and linking them with sources of micro-finance they will, in the medium to long term, be better able to access and own land. Once women have better access to land, women will be in a more favourable position to feed themselves and their families, be able to make decisions on how to use the land, what crops and non-food crops to grow, as well as what to do with the harvest and income generated.

description.narrative: SDG indicator 5.5.1 under (a) measures the proportion of seats held by women in (a) national parliaments, currently as at 1 January of reporting year, is currently measured as the number of seats held by women members in single or lower chambers of national parliaments, expressed as a percentage of all occupied seats. National parliaments can be bicameral or unicameral. This indicator covers the single chamber in unicameral parliaments and the lower chamber in bicameral parliaments. It does not cover the upper chamber of bicameral parliaments. Seats are usually won by members in general parliamentary elections. Seats may also be filled by nomination, appointment, indirect election, rotation of members and byelection. Seats refer to the number of parliamentary mandates, or the number of members of parliament.Data reported against SDG indicators can be retrieved from the official UN SDG Database and Statistics https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/unsdg.
